blocks.content:
Anti-Defection Law applies to State Legislatures as well.

Introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.

Deciding Authority:
• Speaker (Legislative Assembly)
• Chairman (Legislative Council)
Anti-Defection Law applies to State Legislatures as well.

items: Questions frequently test the amendment year: 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
Note that the deciding authority for defection is the Speaker/Chairman of the respective house, NOT the Governor of the state.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Anti-Defection Law extends its application to State Legislatures.
The law was introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985.
The Speaker is the deciding authority for the Legislative Assembly.
The Chairman is the deciding authority for the Legislative Council.
